$comment: templates/minimal/template.json -- the template the pack names `minimal`. Two of the three stacks it serves have NO fresh-tree form, and say so here rather than in code: a stack whose marker is a wrapper script plus a downloaded jar, or an IDE-authored project document, is one nen cannot write honestly. Those stacks still get this template's CI file from `nen scaffold init`, which is the half that is text.
name: minimal
why: the pack's `scaffoldTemplate: "minimal"` -- nen writes the nen-owned slice (declaration, hook, CI, .gitignore) and the manifest that identifies the stack, and never the native project itself.

ci.body:
# .github/workflows/nen-shu.yml -- written by `nen scaffold`.
#
# Every step below is `nen shu <verb>`, and every argv those verbs run comes
# from THIS repository's own nen/contract.json. Nothing in this file names a
# build tool, a package manager or a test runner, and nothing in it should:
# to change what CI runs, change the declaration.
name: nen shu

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  shu:
    runs-on: {{runner}}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Pinned by ref. Re-pinning this repository is this one value; the
      # bootstrap verifies the binary it fetches against the release manifest.
      - name: nen
        env:
          NEN_REF: {{nenRef}}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zheref/nen/${NEN_REF}/bootstrap/nen.sh" -o nen-bootstrap.sh
          echo "NEN=$(bash nen-bootstrap.sh --ref "${NEN_REF}")" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

      # Read-only: reports what this runner has against what the declaration
      # pins, and installs nothing. Exit 5 is "a pinned tool is missing".
      - name: toolchain
        run: |
          "${NEN}" shu tools --repo .

      # --dry-run FIRST on every verb. It prints the argv the declaration
      # states and spawns nothing, so a declaration that drifted fails here
      # rather than half-way through a real build.
      - name: build / test / lint
        run: |
          set +e
          for verb in build test lint; do
            # The empty second form is deliberately unquoted: it must vanish.
            for form in "--dry-run" ""; do
              "${NEN}" shu "${verb}" --repo . ${form}
              status=$?
              [ "${status}" -eq 0 ] && continue
              # 4 is "this lane declares no such verb" -- a fact about the
              # repository, not a failure of the run.
              [ "${status}" -eq 4 ] && { echo "shu ${verb}: not declared for this lane"; break; }
              exit "${status}"
            done
          done

shared..gitignore:
# Written by `nen scaffold new`. nen/ holds committed configuration;
# .nen/ is where every nen verb writes generated output, and it is never
# committed -- the one-character difference is what keeps a build log out of
# a review.
.nen/

postSteps: name the package manager in package.json's "packageManager" field. nen never picks one, so until it is there every declared row that needs it stays a withheld seat
add the framework and its dependencies to package.json, then install them
generate the native ios/ and android/ directories -- nen never templates them, and until they exist the native lanes are not real

gradle-android.noFreshTree: this stack's marker is a wrapper SCRIPT PLUS A DOWNLOADED JAR, and a jar is not something nen can write or verify. Create the project with its own generator, then run `nen scaffold init --repo <path> --stack gradle-android`, which adds every file this template carries except the tree itself.

xcode-ios.noFreshTree: nen never generates an IDE project document. Create the project in the IDE (or with a generator of your own), then run `nen scaffold init --repo <path> --stack xcode-ios`, which adds every file this template carries except the tree itself.
